subject: history
title: Berlin Blockade and the Birth of NATO
welcome_lead: Climb aboard a C-47 over Tempelhof: discover how the Berlin Airlift defied the Soviet blockade and welded the Western alliance.
meta_desc: History Cold War Adventure 2: Berlin Blockade 1948-49, the Airlift and the founding of NATO.
final_note: You have followed the Cold War's first major confrontation. NATO and the Warsaw Pact would soon define a divided Europe.

concepts.def: Soviet closure of road, rail and canal access to West Berlin from 24 June 1948 to 12 May 1949.
Allied operation supplying West Berlin by air, delivering over 2.3 million tons of cargo.
New West German currency introduced June 1948, triggering Soviet objections.
North Atlantic Treaty Organization founded 4 April 1949 by 12 members for collective defence.
Soviet-led military alliance founded 14 May 1955 in response to West Germany joining NATO.
Merged British-American and later French occupation zones in western Germany, foreshadowing the FRG.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Western Allies' introduction of the Deutsche Mark and their plans to build a West German state alarmed Stalin. Hoping to force concessions, the USSR cut surface access to West Berlin on 24 June 1948. The Allies refused to abandon the city or to renegotiate the wider settlement.

From 26 June 1948 the US and Britain organised round-the-clock flights into Tempelhof and Gatow airports. At its peak, planes landed every 30 seconds. After more than 270,000 sorties and over 2.3 million tons of supplies — including the famous 'Candy Bomber' chocolate drops — Stalin lifted the blockade on 12 May 1949.

The blockade accelerated Western unity. The North Atlantic Treaty was signed on 4 April 1949 by Belgium, Britain, Canada, Denmark, France, Iceland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal and the USA. Article 5 enshrined collective defence. The Soviets responded by founding Comecon (1949) and, when West Germany joined NATO in 1955, the Warsaw Pact.
